name: math
algorithm: One std.math function (the variant's name) over 4,096 inputs built from splitmix64 bits in a fixed exponent range, reps passes, each language's standard library; the checksum adds bits >> 32 of each f64 result (bits >> 16 of each f32 result) with wrapping adds, so libraries that differ by an ulp still agree (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the task has no other integer arithmetic

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; each function's accuracy is the lane's Go tests' (TestSTDMATH_TrueError, TestSTDMATH_Exhaustive)

variants.name: fma
notes: Publish reps 650000 so Go's cell runs over 1 s; its checksum is the per-pass sum times reps, the rule every other variant's publish checksum met in verify -publish-size. Go's math.FMA uses the FMA instruction chosen at run time, and on Windows nothing turns that off (GODEBUG=cpu.fma=off is read only on Unix-like systems, README.md), so Go's cell is not x86-64-v2 code; the C and Rust cells run the UCRT's software fma (FMA3 paths off, SM2-R1, SM2-R2).

C is the platform C library (the static UCRT on Windows, glibc on Linux); Rust's f64 and f32 methods call the same library on Windows; both turn the UCRT's run-time FMA3 choice off first (_set_FMA3_enable(0), checked), so the Windows C and Rust cells are x86-64-v2 code (README.md). Zig's @exp, @log, @sin and std.math are Zig's own code; Go's math has no f32 functions, so its f32 rows convert through f64.
Mk's std.math is pure Mk with no cpu dispatch (D8-5), so its fma is a software routine on every target; Sinh and Atan2 run on double-double kernels (std/math/dd.mk) to stay faithfully rounded.

All seven columns (mk, c, rust, rust-ovf, zig-fast, zig-safe, go) agree on the checksum of every variant at the quick size and at the publish size on the owner's machine (go run ./tools/bench verify and verify -publish-size, std-math2 session 2, 2026-11-12); the publish checksums are the per-pass sum times reps, since every pass adds the same sum.
Publish reps are set so the fastest column of each variant ran about 1.2 s or more in the provisional verify -publish-size run (tests/bench/README.md's 1 s floor).
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
